neighbours.label: Verb announcing the outcome of an official decision or selection: 'has been approved', 'was selected', 'the board decided' (also the end of a clause reporting such a decision)
fire: The planning committee confirmed that the new stadium has been approved after two years of debate.
We are happy to tell you that your photograph was selected for the summer exhibition.
Following a public consultation, the school board decided to keep the library open.
The ministry said the merger of the two banks has been approved by regulators.
Our town is proud to have been selected as the host of next year's festival.
After months of protests, the council decided to cancel the road project.
The grant application from the museum was approved by the foundation on Monday.
Her design has been selected by the jury as the winner of the competition.
quiet: The planning committee confirmed that the new stadium has been discussed for two years.
We are sorry to tell you that your photograph was damaged during the summer exhibition.
Following a public consultation, the school board members went home for the weekend.
The ministry said the merger of the two banks has been debated by regulators.
Our town is proud to have been visited by thousands of tourists every festival.
After months of protests, the council members were tired and wanted a holiday.
The grant application from the museum was mailed to the foundation on Monday.
Her design has been copied by rivals since the end of the competition.

notes: Card: ' approved', ' selected', ' decided', and clause ends after decisions (abandoned its tax plans). Probes: approved 0.44, selected 0.55, decided 0.38, abandoned-plans '.' 0.67; 'have been discussed' 0.08, 'has been lost' 0.16.
